title: The Dungeon Map
tagline: the capstone begins - a world made of characters
hints: The map is a `std::vector<std::string>`. `rows_[y][x]` is the character at column x, row y - y FIRST, because y picks the string and x picks the character in it.
In the constructor, build rows_ then scan every tile for '@'. When you find it, save x and y into startX_/startY_ and overwrite that tile with '.', so the map itself holds no player.
`tileAt` must check bounds BEFORE indexing: `if (x < 0 || y < 0 || x >= width() || y >= height()) return '#';` Treating outside-the-map as solid rock means nothing else ever has to worry about it.
`height()` is `rows_.size()`, `width()` is `rows_[0].size()`. Both return int here, so cast: `return (int)rows_.size();`
`render` prints each row character by character, except that when x and y match the player it prints '@' instead. Do not modify rows_ to draw the player - draw over it.
